**AI’s heretical question**

Cryptocurrencies go back to the digital-gold, [sovereign-individual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sovereign_Individual) era of the nineties. People like [Nick Szabo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Szabo) and subcultures like the [cypherpunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cypherpunk) asked a simple, heretical question: “What actually is *money*, and why can’t it be *this*?” That question didn’t *need* [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis) to exist. There was already a minority coalescing around it. But the financial crash of 2008 made it a mainstream concern.

The events of 2008 provided the [counter-positioning of Bitcoin](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/g/genesis-block.asp) and empowered Ethereum, [the extensible world computer](https://ethereum.org/). The heretical question plus the crisis event generated swarms of missionaries and mercenaries, coupling the dynamics of [unregulated finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legality_of_cryptocurrency_by_country_or_territory) with the rollout of novel, [globally distributed cryptographic infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain).

The same pattern is playing out in computing and intelligence right now.

The capital behind AI isn’t cute SaaS cheques. It’s government-balance-sheet money. Trillions are on the line. And for good reason; the capabilities (realised and latent) are astounding. So states are starting to treat compute the way they used to treat oil: a strategic asset to subsidise, hoard, and secure the supply chains for. Their defence budgets are really a bet on autonomous systems. Autonomous systems are themselves a bet on AI. And AI, right now, runs on exactly *one* computing paradigm. A [foundation from the fifties](https://steveblank.com/secret-history/).

That paradigm is young. Silicon, transistors, the von Neumann architecture; the whole engineered stack is eighty-ish years old. It is not physical law.

Young means revisable. Open to change. Quantum, analog, thermodynamic, biophysical; these alternative paradigms aren’t sci-fi, or cope. They have heritage. They’re [evolutionary branches](https://worldmachines.org/evolution/) that got KO’d early and are now being reevaluated because the stakes are *colossal*.

Whether [scaling](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2026-06-24-scaling-laws/) does in fact hit a wall or not is irrelevant. This much money and this much power riding on one bet practically guarantees that someone, somewhere, will go back and double-check the foundations, and discover alternatives with surer routes to victory. Which is what this is ultimately about. *Victory*.

Cryptocurrencies blew up because an explosive, heretical question boomed off the back of world economic pressure.  Entire non-Von-Neumann computing and intelligence stacks, from base hardware to edge applications, are under arguably greater pressure today. But unlike crypto, which didn’t manage to unseat the Goliath of fiat with a parallel buildout, alternative computing and intelligence paradigms might have the power to catalyse a straight and irreversible cutover.
